claims.text: Adding a controlled low volume fraction of finely dispersed oxide nanoparticles such as Y2O3 will improve the high-temperature mechanical properties of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The oxide addition will not significantly increase the alloy density.
The oxide addition will not adversely affect room-temperature mechanical performance.
The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy has balanced room-temperature strength and toughness.
The baseline alloy has limited high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance.
Adding nano-oxides during processing can produce a uniform in situ dispersion in the alloy matrix.
The oxide nanoparticle dispersion will remain stable and homogeneous at approximately 800–1000 °C under sustained loading.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles will pin dislocations.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries.
A controlled oxide dispersion can avoid phase separation and agglomeration.
The oxide nanoparticles act as precipitation-strengthening agents by impeding dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
The low density of the oxide addition minimizes its effect on overall alloy density.
The oxide nanoparticles will not significantly hinder dislocation activity at room temperature.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will exhibit approximately 15–25% greater high-temperature yield strength than the unmodified baseline alloy.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will exhibit approximately 15–25% improved creep resistance relative to the unmodified baseline alloy.
Excessive oxide content may cause agglomeration.
Excessive oxide content may increase density.
Excessive oxide content may embrittle the alloy.
The magnitude of improvement depends on processing parameters and operating conditions.
